question: Find me stocks that dropped a lot lately but the company is actually fine — still growing revenue, and not overpriced. Dip-buy candidates.

q: big price drawdown from recent high
price down sharply over the last few months

queries: valuation below the sector average / not expensive

technical_evidence_key: matched.ta  (the price-drop signal is keyed by its human label, e.g. matched.ta["price net drop ≥20%"], whose .detail.ret holds the drop fraction)
both_legs_populated: YES — both legs carry real, non-empty evidence. Examples: ACIC.US: matched.ta['price net drop ≥20%'].detail.ret = -0.2294 (down ~22.9%); matched.fundamental.revenue.series=[0.1301,0.1242] (revenue grew +13.0% then +12.4% YoY, min_yoy value 0.1242); matched.fundamental.pe.value=4.68 vs cohort_benchmark=18.12 (own_sector) → cheap. ACM.US (Aecom): ret=-0.2038 (-20.4%), revenue growth series [0.0021,0.1201], pe.value=28.41 vs cohort 35.36. head 1752 (gross_margin 0.80 name hidden in preview): ret=-0.235 (-23.5%), revenue series [0.6519,0.2297], pe.value=39.13 vs cohort 61.92.
answer_to_user: I found ~40 dip-buy candidates that satisfy ALL THREE conditions at once: (1) price is down ~20%+ recently, (2) revenue grew every year over the last 2 years, and (3) P/E sits below its own sector's average (i.e. not overpriced relative to peers). Top examples: American Coastal Insurance (ACIC.US) — down ~23%, revenue +12–13%/yr, P/E 4.7 vs a sector avg of 18.1 (very cheap, normalized_pe 4.5, net margin 30%); AECOM (ACM.US) — down ~20%, revenue still growing, P/E 28.4 vs sector 35.4; and a ~$31bn high-gross-margin (80%) name down ~23.5% with revenue up 23–65%/yr, P/E 39 vs a sector avg of 62. Each row carries the exact drop %, the revenue-growth series, and the P/E-vs-peer-average that qualified it, so you can vet them. Note: 'not overpriced' here means cheap RELATIVE TO its own sector (cohort), not an absolute low-P/E cutoff.
